title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 55
paragraphs: The reason I have mentioned this I will now explain. In this Acropolis there is a temple of Erechtheus, who is said to have been born of the Earth, and in it there is an olive tree and a sea which (according to the story told by the Athenians) Poseidon and Athena, when they contended for the land, set up as their witnesses. Now this olive tree had been set on fire along with the rest of the temple by the barbarians. But on the day after the conflagration, those Athenians who had been ordered by the king to offer sacrifice, when they had gone up to the temple, saw that a shoot had grown up from the stump about a cubit in length. These men duly reported it.
